title: Client-aware emergency shedding with shardless rate decay
creator: Marco Chen
description:
Problem: Recent incidents show that when the central quota shard becomes unavailable (partial region partition or limiter process crash) traffic either stalls or is reverted to very coarse global throttles, causing large SLO violations for latency-sensitive hosted API customers. We need an emergency degradation mode that preserves SLOs for latency and fairness across customers while avoiding dangerous over-issuance of tokens during attack-like bursts.

Goal: Implement a shardless emergency shedding algorithm that runs in the edge/routing layer to approximate per-customer allowances using short-window exponential decay of recent usage, traffic sampling, and SLO-weighted prioritization. The mechanism should be safe as a temporary fallback (<30s steady state), auditable in logs, and reversible when normal quota service resumes.

Design summary:
- Edge maintains a rolling EWMA usage estimate per customer and per-route (configurable decay half-life, default 10s) using sampled tokens from the normal token stream to bound memory and CPU.
- When central limiter is unreachable for >150ms, edges enter EMERGENCY_SHED mode and compute a shardless allowance: max(min(baseline_quota, ewma_capacity * safety_factor), emergency_floor).
- Safety factors differ by tier: 0.6 (P0 customers), 0.4 (P1), 0.25 (P2/P3). Emergency floor prevents total starvation for small customers.
- Fairness: allowances scaled by recent 1-minute usage percentile to avoid large tenants consuming reclaimed capacity. Also include a short randomized jitter to reduce synchronized retries.
- Circuit breaker and rehydration: edges attempt periodic health-checks to central limiter; on heal, they linearly ramp down shardless allowances over 10s and reconcile real tokens via a reconciliation protocol to avoid accidental double-issuance.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Pros: preserves latency SLOs for most customers during short limiter outages, predictable bounded over-issuance, works without involving centralized state.
- Cons: approximation may under-serve very bursty but healthy customers; malicious actors could attempt to game EWMA windows (mitigation: heavier sampling for anomalous clients and adaptive safety factors). Complexity added to edge routing code and observability surface.

Acceptance criteria:
- Edges enter EMERGENCY_SHED mode automatically when central limiter unreachable >150ms.
- During staged failure testing, 95th percentile p99 latency for hosted API remains within SLO target + 30% while total token over-issuance across a 60s outage remains <10% for P0 customers and <5% for P1.
- Reconciliation avoids any duplicate token assignment in 99.99% of simulated recovery scenarios.
- Monitoring dashboards for mode transitions, per-customer emergency allowance, and over-issuance rate exist and are visible in Console (linked below).

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Telemetry & sampling: add sampled token stream to routing service (2 engineers, 2d). Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RTE/Shardless+Limiter+Design
2) Edge EWMA store: implement sharded in-memory sliding EWMA with LRU eviction and bounds (3 engineers, 4d).
3) Emergency mode state machine + safety factors (2 engineers, 3d). Add config flags for tier safety overrides.
4) Reconciliation protocol: idempotent recovery handshake between edge and limiter to consume outstanding in-flight allowances (3 engineers, 4d). Refer to PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/limiter/pull/1882
5) Integration tests and chaos testing in staging (1 engineer, 3d). See chaos playbook: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Emu-sim-playbook
6) Observability: dashboards and alerts (1 engineer, 2d). Dashboards: LIMITER/EmergencyMode, LIMITER/OverissuanceByTier.

Rollout plan:
- Feature flag gated by project and route. Start with internal tenants -> canary customers -> all hosted API.
- Metric gates for promotion: <2% emergency mode total time across canary, over-issuance within targets, and no SLO regressions on traced requests.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for EWMA math and LRU eviction.
- Simulation harness that replays production token traces to validate allowance bounds under attack scenarios (link: https://internal.redwood.ai/datasets/token-traces).
- Staged chaos: induce limiter partition in staging across us-east-1 and eu-west-1 and validate cross-region behavior and reconciliation.

Open questions:
- Exact decay half-life value (A/B test of 5s vs 10s in sim harness).
- How to incorporate KV-cache hits into allowance computation (proposal: treat cache-hit routes as having a smaller safety factor).
- Whether to persist sampled EWMA to disk for very long outages (current plan: memory-only to avoid complexity).
